description: An introduction to why atoms combine and how ionic, covalent and metallic bonds form, including the octet rule and the properties of the compounds produced.

mcq.questionText: Why do most atoms combine with other atoms to form chemical bonds?

options.text: To gain a stable electron arrangement like that of a noble gas
To increase the number of neutrons in the nucleus
To lose all of their electrons

mcq.explanation: Atoms bond in order to attain a full, stable outer shell similar to the nearest noble gas, which lowers their energy.

mcq.questionText: The tendency of atoms to achieve eight electrons in their outermost shell is called the:
mcq.explanation: The octet rule states that atoms tend to gain, lose or share electrons to obtain eight electrons in their outermost shell.

mcq.questionText: Which type of bond is formed by the complete transfer of electrons from one atom to another?
mcq.explanation: In ionic bonding electrons are transferred from a metal to a non-metal, forming oppositely charged ions that attract each other.

mcq.questionText: When sodium reacts with chlorine to form sodium chloride, the sodium atom:

options.text: Gains one electron to form Na-
Loses one electron to form Na+
Loses two electrons to form Na2+

mcq.explanation: Sodium has one outer electron which it loses to chlorine, becoming a positively charged ion (Na+).

mcq.questionText: A covalent bond is best described as the:

options.text: Transfer of electrons between two metals
Sharing of one or more pairs of electrons between atoms
Attraction between positive ions and free electrons
Loss of electrons by a non-metal

mcq.explanation: A covalent bond forms when two atoms, usually non-metals, share pairs of electrons to fill their outer shells.

mcq.questionText: How many pairs of electrons are shared in a molecule of methane (CH4)?
mcq.explanation: Carbon shares its four outer electrons with four hydrogen atoms, forming four shared pairs (four single covalent bonds).

mcq.questionText: Which of the following is a property typical of ionic compounds?

options.text: They conduct electricity when molten or dissolved in water
They are usually gases at room temperature
They do not dissolve in water

mcq.explanation: Ionic compounds conduct electricity when molten or in solution because their ions become free to move and carry charge.

mcq.questionText: Metallic bonding is described as the attraction between:

options.text: Positive metal ions and a sea of delocalised electrons
Positive and negative ions in a lattice

mcq.explanation: In metals, positive ions are surrounded by a sea of mobile (delocalised) electrons whose attraction holds the structure together.

mcq.questionText: Why do metals conduct electricity well?

options.text: Their ions can move easily in the solid
They are made of covalent molecules

mcq.explanation: The delocalised electrons in a metal are free to move throughout the structure and carry electric current.

mcq.questionText: In the formation of magnesium oxide (MgO), how many electrons does a magnesium atom transfer?
mcq.explanation: Magnesium has two outer electrons which it transfers to oxygen, forming Mg2+ and O2- ions.

mcq.questionText: Which statement correctly compares ionic and covalent compounds?

options.text: Ionic compounds usually have higher melting points than simple covalent compounds
Covalent compounds always conduct electricity better than ionic compounds
Ionic compounds are always gases while covalent compounds are solids
Both types never dissolve in water

mcq.explanation: Strong electrostatic forces in ionic lattices need much energy to break, giving ionic compounds high melting points compared with simple covalent substances.

mcq.questionText: How many electrons are shared in the double bond of an oxygen molecule (O2)?
mcq.explanation: A double bond consists of two shared pairs, which means four electrons are shared between the two oxygen atoms.

mcq.questionText: Which atom achieves a duplet (two electrons) rather than an octet when it forms bonds?
mcq.explanation: Hydrogen needs only two electrons to fill its single shell, so it follows the duplet rule rather than the octet rule.

mcq.questionText: Why does solid sodium chloride NOT conduct electricity, while molten sodium chloride does?

options.text: In the solid the ions are fixed in place, but in the molten state they are free to move
The solid contains no ions at all
Melting changes the ions into neutral atoms

mcq.explanation: Conduction needs mobile charge carriers; in the solid lattice ions cannot move, but when molten the ions are free to carry current.

mcq.questionText: An element with electron arrangement 2,8,7 is most likely to form a chemical bond by:

options.text: Gaining one electron to complete its octet

mcq.explanation: With seven outer electrons the atom needs only one more to reach a stable octet, so it tends to gain one electron and become a 1- ion.

fib.questionText: The chemical bond formed when electrons are completely transferred from a metal to a non-metal is called an _____ bond.
fib.explanation: Ionic (electrovalent) bonding involves the transfer of electrons, producing oppositely charged ions.

fib.questionText: Atoms tend to gain, lose or share electrons in order to obtain a stable arrangement similar to that of a _____ gas.
fib.explanation: Noble gases have full, stable outer shells, which other atoms try to imitate when bonding.

fib.questionText: A bond formed by the sharing of pairs of electrons between atoms is a _____ bond.
fib.explanation: Covalent bonding occurs mainly between non-metal atoms that share electrons.

fib.questionText: The rule that states atoms try to attain eight electrons in their outer shell is called the _____ rule.
fib.explanation: The octet rule explains why many atoms gain, lose or share electrons to reach eight in the outer shell.

fib.questionText: In sodium chloride, the sodium ion carries a charge of _____ (write the sign and number).
fib.explanation: Sodium loses one electron to become Na+, a single positive charge.

fib.questionText: In metallic bonding, the metal atoms are held together by a sea of _____ electrons.
fib.explanation: Delocalised (free) electrons move throughout the metal and attract the positive metal ions.

fib.questionText: Hydrogen needs only two electrons to fill its shell, so it follows the _____ rule.
fib.explanation: Hydrogen and helium are stable with two electrons, an arrangement known as the duplet.

fib.questionText: Compounds with simple covalent molecules generally have _____ (high/low) melting points compared with ionic compounds.
fib.explanation: Weak forces between separate covalent molecules are easily broken, giving low melting points.

fib.questionText: An ion that carries a negative charge is called an _____.
fib.explanation: Atoms that gain electrons become negatively charged ions called anions.

fib.questionText: In a water molecule (H2O), oxygen forms _____ covalent bonds with hydrogen atoms.
fib.explanation: Oxygen shares one electron with each of two hydrogen atoms, forming two single covalent bonds.

tf.questionText: Atoms form chemical bonds in order to become more stable.
tf.explanation: Bonding lets atoms achieve a stable, full outer shell and lower energy.

tf.questionText: Ionic bonding occurs mainly between two non-metal atoms.
tf.explanation: Ionic bonding usually occurs between a metal and a non-metal; covalent bonding occurs between non-metals.

tf.questionText: In a covalent bond, electrons are shared rather than transferred.
tf.explanation: Covalent bonding involves the sharing of electron pairs between atoms.

tf.questionText: Ionic compounds conduct electricity when they are in the solid state.
tf.explanation: Ionic solids do not conduct because the ions are fixed; they conduct only when molten or dissolved.

tf.questionText: Metals are generally good conductors of electricity because of their free-moving electrons.
tf.explanation: Delocalised electrons in metals move freely and carry electric current.

tf.questionText: When sodium forms a bond with chlorine, sodium gains an electron.
tf.explanation: Sodium loses one electron to chlorine; it is chlorine that gains an electron.

tf.questionText: A double covalent bond involves the sharing of two pairs of electrons.
tf.explanation: A double bond consists of two shared electron pairs, as seen in the oxygen molecule.

tf.questionText: Ionic compounds usually have higher melting points than simple covalent compounds.
tf.explanation: Strong electrostatic forces in ionic lattices require a lot of energy to overcome.

tf.questionText: Hydrogen obeys the octet rule by gaining eight electrons when it bonds.
tf.explanation: Hydrogen obeys the duplet rule, needing only two electrons to fill its single shell.

tf.questionText: Most simple covalent compounds do not conduct electricity because they contain no free ions or electrons.
tf.explanation: Covalent molecules are neutral and have no mobile charge carriers, so they generally do not conduct.

summary.correctAnswer: To gain a stable, full outer shell like a noble gas
summary.explanation: Stability is achieved by completing the outermost electron shell.

summary.correctAnswer: Atoms tend to achieve eight electrons in their outer shell
summary.explanation: This drives the gaining, losing or sharing of electrons.

summary.correctAnswer: Hydrogen and helium are stable with two outer electrons
summary.explanation: Small atoms with one shell only need two electrons to be stable.

summary.correctAnswer: Transfer of electrons from a metal to a non-metal forming ions
summary.explanation: Oppositely charged ions attract to form the compound, e.g. NaCl.

summary.correctAnswer: Sharing of electron pairs between non-metal atoms
Attraction between positive metal ions and delocalised electrons
summary.explanation: This explains why metals conduct and are malleable.

summary.correctAnswer: Conduct only when molten or dissolved in water
summary.explanation: Ions must be free to move to carry current.

summary.correctAnswer: Generally high due to strong electrostatic forces
summary.explanation: Much energy is needed to break the ionic lattice.

summary.correctAnswer: Low melting points and usually do not conduct electricity
summary.explanation: Weak forces between molecules and no free charges.

summary.correctAnswer: A cation is a positive ion; an anion is a negative ion
summary.explanation: Cations form by losing electrons, anions by gaining electrons.

hoq.questionText: An element X has electron arrangement 2,8,2 and element Y has 2,8,7. What type of bond and formula will they most likely form?
hoq.explanation: X loses 2 electrons (X2+) and each Y gains 1 (Y-), so two Y ions balance one X ion giving the ionic formula XY2.

hoq.questionText: Carbon dioxide (CO2) has low melting point and does not conduct electricity, while magnesium oxide (MgO) has a very high melting point and conducts when molten. What does this difference best indicate?

options.text: CO2 is covalent while MgO is ionic
CO2 is metallic while MgO is covalent

hoq.explanation: Low melting point and non-conduction point to simple covalent CO2, while a high melting point and conduction when molten point to ionic MgO.

hoq.questionText: Why can metals be hammered into sheets (malleable) without breaking, unlike ionic solids which shatter?

options.text: Metal layers can slide over each other while the sea of electrons keeps them bonded
Metals contain no bonds at all so atoms move freely
Metals are made of small covalent molecules that flow
Metal ions repel each other when struck, spreading the metal out

hoq.explanation: Layers of metal ions slide past one another while the delocalised electrons maintain the bonding, so metals deform instead of shattering, whereas in ionic solids like charges align and repel.
